title: Release purchase orders to production
body:
PRs #28 and #29 are merged; per PR #28, production was at migration 39.

- [ ] Run migrations 40–43 against a copy of prod data and check the suppliers the backfill creates
- [ ] Check prod's roles are named Cashier, Manager and Admin (migration 43 grants by name, see T-099)
- [ ] Click through what #29's Playwright checks skipped: the admin category and permission delete dialogs, and the sales page "Discard and continue" path
- [ ] `make assets`, build the image, deploy, have every user log in again to pick up the new permissions

title: Authenticate the /ws WebSocket
body: `/ws` bypasses the middleware stack and `HandleWebSocket` never checks the session, so anyone can subscribe to stock-taking updates. Check the session (and tenant) before upgrading.

title: Validate sale prices server-side
body: `CreateSale` stores the client-sent `unit_price`, `discount`, `total` and `subtotal` as-is. Re-price from `product_price`, recompute totals, and enforce discount rules on the server.

title: Fix money conversion rounding
body: Amounts arrive as float naira and are converted with `int(x * 100)`, which truncates (e.g. 0.29 → 28 kobo). Send kobo integers from the client, or round explicitly.

title: Prevent negative stock on sale
body:
`CreateSale` posts `OUT_SALE` without checking available stock. Block or require an override permission when a sale exceeds stock.

The check has to lock the products first, the way stock adjustments do (`LockProductStockTx`: `FOR UPDATE` in id order, then read stock in a second statement). Until sales take that lock, a sale committing at the same moment as an adjustment isn't counted by the adjustment's below-zero check.

title: Re-check permissions on each request
body:
Permissions are cached in the session cookie at login (`RequirePermissions` reads `session.Values["permissions"]`), so revoking a role or permission only takes effect after re-login or the 3am expiry. Load from DB (cached briefly) per request; add a way to end a user's sessions.

Since T-050 a signed-out API call gets 401 JSON. Add one shared handler in the SPA: on a 401, show "You've been signed out. Sign in again" with a link, keep the page's state, and stop the badge polls. Today only Stock Adjustments shows the server's message; other screens say "Server error (401)" or "Failed to load data".

title: Login rate limiting & cookie hardening
body:
No throttling or lockout on failed logins. Session cookie lacks `Secure`; review `SameSite`. Add HTTPS-only settings and security headers.

Also cap request body size on every JSON endpoint (one middleware or shared helper). T-018 added `decodeLimitedJSON` (16 KB, 413 when exceeded) to the admin create-user and reset-password handlers only.

title: Sign-in can send you to a stale page
body: `AuthMiddleware` stores the page you were trying to open in the session as `next`, and sign-in sends you there. Visiting `/user/logout` while signed out stores `/user/logout`, and the next sign-in then lands on a 404. An API call made after the session ends (an open page's background fetch) does the same, and sign-in then shows raw JSON. Ignore `next` for sign-out and clear it after use. (Since T-050, API calls get a 401 and are no longer saved as `next`; the sign-out case remains.) Found in T-050's browser check.

title: Sales and receipts during a stock take are counted twice
body: A product's stock is snapshotted the first time it's counted in a stock taking, and completing the taking posts (count - snapshot). A sale or receipt of that product between its count and completion is in both the movements and the difference: snapshot 50, sell 5, count 45 → completion posts −5, stock ends at 40 with 45 on the shelf. Stock adjustments refuse products already counted in an open stock taking (T-050); sales and receiving don't. Either move the snapshot by every movement after it, or snapshot at count time and post (count − stock at count). Recording a count should also lock the product row (as adjustments do), so a count saved at the same moment as an adjustment can't take its snapshot before the adjustment and slip past the adjustment's check. Raised in T-050's review.

title: CI pipeline
body: GitHub Actions: `go test ./...` with Postgres (integration tests), `gofmt`/golines checks, `go vet`, frontend build, Docker build.

title: Automated backups & restore
body:
Nothing in the repo or the compose setup makes backups. Start with the single store, then grow into the hosted version.

- [ ] Daily `pg_dump` on the store machine, kept for a set number of days, compressed
- [ ] Copy each backup automatically to a fixed location set in config (shared folder, external drive, Google Drive / Dropbox / S3)
- [ ] Share a backup on demand by any available means (download from the admin screen, OS share sheet, email or WhatsApp the file)
- [ ] Last-backup status and a warning in the admin screen when a backup fails or is overdue
- [ ] Documented, tested restore
- [ ] Hosted: point-in-time recovery, off-site copies, per-tenant data export

title: Health check, graceful shutdown & observability
body: No `/healthz`, `server.ListenAndServe()` with no graceful shutdown or timeouts, logs only to a local `app.log`. Add health/readiness endpoints, structured logging to stdout, error tracking (e.g. Sentry), uptime monitoring and metrics.

title: Runtime configuration
body: Config comes from `config/.env` embedded at build time (`//go:embed .env`), so secrets and settings are baked into the binary. Read from real environment variables or a secrets manager at runtime; one image for every environment.

title: Multi-tenancy architecture
body: Every table is global today; one deployment = one store. Decide the isolation model (shared schema with `tenant_id` + row-level security, schema-per-tenant, or DB-per-tenant), then add tenant scoping to all queries, sessions and the WebSocket hub, and tenant resolution (subdomain or custom domain).

title: Store settings & white-label branding
body:
"Primocrest Pharmacy" is hardcoded in the receipt (`composables/usePos.js`), `Sidebar.vue`, `LoginPage.vue`, `NotFoundPage.vue` and the `<title>` of `login-v2.html`, `next-dashboard.html` and `error.html`. Add per-store settings and use them everywhere:

- [ ] Name, logo or icon (replacing the text-only brand mark)
- [ ] Receipt header and footer: address, phone
- [ ] Primary colour (brand tokens are in the Tailwind theme and `design-system/primocrest-pharmacy/MASTER.md`; status colours stay fixed so green, amber and red keep their meaning)
- [ ] Timezone (the dashboard uses server local time) and currency

Stored with the other settings from T-093.

title: Bulk product import (CSV/Excel)
body: Import products, prices, price options and opening stock with expiry from a spreadsheet, with validation preview and error report. The biggest onboarding blocker for a new store.

title: Tenant signup & onboarding wizard
body:
Self-serve signup that creates a tenant and its first admin, then a guided setup: store details, categories, products (import), users, opening stock.

First-admin creation moves here from the `create-admin` command (T-018) once a new store is set up in the app.

title: Subscription billing & plans
body: Plans, trials, recurring billing (Paystack/Flutterwave for NGN), dunning, plan limits (users, products, branches) and feature gating.

title: Super-admin console
body: Platform operator view: tenants, plans and billing status, usage, suspend/reactivate, support impersonation (audited).

title: Online-first with solid offline operation
body:
Run against a hosted server, but losing the connection must never stall work. Today every screen stops when the network or server drops.

- [ ] Local cache of products, prices and stock, refreshed in the background
- [ ] Sales, returns, receiving and stock counts saved locally and queued while offline (idempotency keys already exist for sales and receiving)
- [ ] Sync as soon as the connection returns, with retry and a visible pending count
- [ ] Clear online/offline indicator; reprint and hold work offline
- [ ] Conflict rules: stock going negative across devices, prices changed while offline, a held sale resumed on two tills
- [ ] Decide the offline store (service worker + IndexedDB, or the desktop app in T-094)

title: Audit log everything
body:
Every change writes an `audit_log` entry in the same transaction: who, when, what, before and after, and a reason where it matters. Only purchase orders do this today. Add a shared `auditEntry` helper in the service layer.

- [ ] Sales, voids, returns and refunds
- [ ] Stock movements: receiving, manual adjustments, stock-take completion
- [ ] Product, price and cost edits; categories, groups and merges
- [ ] Users, roles and permissions; logins, logouts and failed logins
- [ ] Settings changes and data exports
- [ ] Admin screen to browse, filter (user, entity, action, date) and export the log

Password resets by an admin are not audited yet (T-018 audits user creation only); include them here.

title: Granular permissions with default roles
body:
Everything is behind a permission. The system ships with default roles that have permissions assigned, and every permission has an explanation.

- [ ] Permission catalog in code: key, name, description, group (Sales, Inventory, Purchasing, Reports, Admin…)
- [ ] Every route and every UI action checks a permission. Today many are ungated: creating products (`POST /inventory/add-item`), receiving, sales, returns, stock-take create and count, and most read endpoints
- [ ] Default roles seeded by migration and kept in sync with the catalog (e.g. Owner, Manager, Pharmacist, Cashier, Storekeeper)
- [ ] Admin screen lists permissions grouped, with their explanations, and lets admins build custom roles from the catalog
- [ ] Remove the free-form create/delete permission endpoints; permissions are defined by code
- [ ] Decide the purchase order read endpoints: list, get and history have no route permission (the service only hides drafts from people who aren't the author or an approver)
- [ ] Decide whether receiving against a purchase order needs its own permission (today anyone who can receive can)
- [ ] Seed grants without matching role names: migration 000043 grants by name (`r.name = 'Cashier'`, `IN ('Manager', 'Admin')`), which breaks when a deployment's roles are named differently or tenants rename them
- [ ] Works with per-request permission checks (T-023)

- [ ] Split user management from `admin:access`: today anyone holding it can add users with any role, including Admin, and change roles. Limit which roles a non-Admin can grant (raised in T-018 review)

title: Password policy toward NIST guidance
body: T-018 set a 10-character minimum, a common-password list and a username check. NIST SP 800-63B rev 4 also asks for at least a 64-character maximum, no composition rules, and a 15-character minimum while login is password-only. Move to 15 when it's workable for the shop or once there's a second factor (T-075).

title: Notification centre
body:
One place for everything the system needs to tell people. Today the only notification is the approver badge and dashboard banner, which poll every 60 seconds (`usePendingPurchaseOrders.js`).

- [ ] Stored in-app inbox with a bell and unread count, per user
- [ ] Events: purchase orders submitted, approved, sent back or rejected (T-089); low stock and upcoming expiry; backup failed (T-026); offline sync problems (T-047); what's new (T-095); insights (T-100)
- [ ] Channels: in-app, email, WhatsApp/SMS, push (desktop and mobile)
- [ ] Per-user and per-role preferences, and a daily digest option

title: Costs on purchase orders

Hard-coded values should become settings that an admin edits on a settings screen. Store them in the database, read them once per session and serve them to the SPA, so the frontend and backend share one value. Store branding (T-030) uses the same store.

The customer name is typed on the receipt but never stored.

body: Sell on account, track customer balances, record part-payments, statements and aged debt. Very common in Nigerian retail.

title: Void / cancel a completed sale
body: No way to void a mistaken sale. Add void with reason, permission and audit entry; reverse stock movements and payments.

Cash control for each till.

- [ ] Open a till session with an opening float; every sale, return and payout belongs to a session
- [ ] Record how each refund was paid out (cash, transfer, store credit); returns only store `total_refunded` today
- [ ] Close with counted cash per payment method, showing expected, counted and over/short

body: Max discount per role, price override requiring permission, promotions (percentage, buy-X-get-Y, time-bound).

title: Keyboard workflow for POS and Receive Items
body:
Make the two busiest screens fully usable without a mouse.

- [ ] POS: focus search (`/` or F2), arrow keys + Enter to add, change quantity and price option, remove a line, discount, choose a payment method, save, save and print, hold

title: Thermal printing & digital receipts
body: ESC/POS thermal printer support (58/80mm), receipts by WhatsApp/SMS/email. Reprint from sales history was split out to T-112.

title: Batch tracking & FEFO
body:
Track stock per batch, not just per product. Today stock is one number per product summed from `stock_movement`, and expiry is the product's earliest date, so you can't tell how much of an expiring batch is actually left.

- [ ] Capture the batch/lot number on receiving: `product_batch.batch_no` exists but `createProductBatchQuery` never writes it
- [ ] Several batches (different expiry dates) on one purchase order line
- [ ] Quantity on hand per batch; sales, returns and adjustments deduct from a batch
- [ ] First-expiry-first-out by default at the POS, with an override
- [ ] Expiry lists and write-offs per batch
- [ ] Recall lookup: which sales (and customers, T-040) took batch X

Per-batch stock adjustments and lot details on write-offs belong here (T-050 adjusts at product level).

title: Multi-store & multi-branch support
body:
One business owns one or more stores, and each store has one or more branches. Dispensary and store room become locations inside a branch (today they exist only as stock-take counts).

- [ ] Stock, batches and stock takes per branch and location
- [ ] Prices shared across branches, with optional branch overrides
- [ ] Users and permissions per branch, and a branch switcher
- [ ] Transfers between branches, with an in-transit state and receipt at the other end
- [ ] Reports per branch, plus an owner view across branches: sales, stock, transfers and branch comparison

title: Product history
body:
One screen per product that shows its whole history:

- [ ] Stock ledger: every receipt, sale, return, adjustment and stock take, with running balance, user and reference
- [ ] Purchase cost history per receipt and supplier (already stored on `product_batch`)
- [ ] Selling price history: prices are updated in place today (`UpdateProduct`), so start recording price changes with who and when
- [ ] Restock dates and quantities, and time between restocks
- [ ] Simple charts for cost, price and stock over time

title: Reorder planning & on-order quantities
body:
Know what to buy and what's already coming.

- [ ] Show quantities on open purchase orders on the Products list and the Low Stock page (today they only appear in the purchase order low-stock picker as "already on order")
- [ ] Suggest reorder quantities from the reorder level (or the group's, T-097), sales rate and supplier lead time, minus what's on order
- [ ] Generate a draft purchase order per supplier from the suggestions

title: Returns to supplier
body: Send expired, damaged or excess stock back to a supplier with a document, stock movement and expected credit.

title: Supplier invoices & payables
body: Record supplier invoices against receipts, amounts owed, payments made and balances per supplier.

title: Product archive & bulk price update
body: Deactivate products without losing history; update prices in bulk (by category or percentage).

title: Product groups with a group reorder level
body:
Group interchangeable products, e.g. different brands of amoxicillin 500mg that all sell at ₦600. A group has its own reorder level and total stock, and low stock is judged on the group as well as on each product. Optional shared group price. Groups feed reorder planning (T-053).

- [ ] Group with its own reorder level, total stock and optional shared price
- [ ] Low stock judged per group as well as per product
- [ ] Substitution at the POS: when a product is out of stock, suggest in-stock products from the same group or with the same active ingredient (T-057)

title: Approval for large stock adjustments
body: Adjustments above a quantity or value threshold wait for a second manager, so the person adjusting isn't the one approving. Threshold set on the settings screen. Raised in T-050.

title: Adjust stock in packs as well as units
body: Stock adjustments are entered in base units. Let the manager pick a price option (pack, sachet) and enter quantities in it. Raised in T-050.

title: Merge duplicate products, categories and groups
body: Pick a surviving record and move everything onto it: stock movements, batches, prices, sales and return lines, purchase order lines, stock-take items. Then remove or archive the duplicate. Preview what moves, require a permission and write an audit entry. Suppliers merge in T-038; groups come from T-097.

title: Pharmacy product attributes
body:
Generic name / active ingredient, strength, dosage form, pack size, NAFDAC number, classification (OTC / POM / controlled).

The POS search already looks for `generic_name` (`pos/ProductPanel.vue`), but the backend has no such field, so that part of the search never matches.

title: Prescriptions & dispensing records
body: Record prescriptions (prescriber, patient, items, directions), link to sales, pharmacist sign-off required for POM items.

title: Controlled drugs register
body: Running register of controlled substances: receipts, dispensing, balances, who did it, for inspections.

title: Sales & profit reports
body:
- [ ] Gross profit and margin by period, product and category, using batch cost (already captured on `product_batch`)
- [ ] Sales by cashier, product, category, payment method and hour
- [ ] End-of-day summary

title: Stock valuation, dead stock & write-off reports
body:
Stock value at cost and retail, slow and dead movers, value of expired / written-off stock.

Write-off value by reason: `stock_adjustment_item.unit_cost_kobo × quantity_change`, grouped by `stock_adjustment.reason` (T-050).

title: More useful sales and inventory metrics
body:
At-a-glance numbers for the dashboard; the full reports are T-060, T-060 and T-062.

- [ ] Sales: gross margin %, average basket value and items per sale, sales by hour and weekday, returns rate, comparison with the same day last week
- [ ] Inventory: stock value at cost, days of cover per product or group, stock turnover, sell-through since receipt, value at risk of expiry, fast movers next to dead stock

title: Business insights
body:
Go beyond tables: have the system point out what matters. The detailed reports are T-060 to T-062; the metrics are T-096.

- [ ] "Runs out in N days at the current sales rate" for each product or group
- [ ] Margin changes, e.g. the last restock cost went up but the selling price didn't
- [ ] Sales up or down against the same weekday or period last time, by product and category
- [ ] Money tied up in slow movers, and stock value at risk of expiry in the next 30/60/90 days
- [ ] Daily and weekly summaries for owners (delivered through T-103)

title: Export data
body:
Get data out in a usable form.

- [ ] CSV/Excel export on every list and report (and relink the existing stock CSV export)
- [ ] Full store export: products, prices, stock and batches, customers, sales, purchases, suppliers, as a zip of CSVs, for accounting, migration or leaving
- [ ] Optional scheduled export to the backup location (T-026)
- [ ] Exports need a permission and are audited (T-035)

title: Admin user management
body: Admins can add users (T-018), but can't deactivate them, and users can't change their own password. Add deactivate, change own password, last login, and optionally invite by link instead of a starting password.

title: Temporary passwords: change on first sign-in
body:
The password an admin sets with Add user or Reset Password is known to the admin, so make it temporary.

- [ ] A `must_change_password` flag on users (migration), set by Add user and admin resets, not by `create-admin`
- [ ] While it's set, every page and API call except change password and sign out sends the user to a "Set your password" screen, enforced on the server
- [ ] The screen asks for the temporary password, a new one and a confirmation. Same rules as everywhere (`ValidatePassword`), and it must differ from the temporary one. Saving clears the flag and writes an audit entry
- [ ] Administration → Users shows "Password not set yet"
- [ ] Optional: temporary passwords expire after a set number of days

Shares the change-password endpoint and screen with T-064's "users change their own password". Build them together. Raised during T-018.

title: Release & deployment pipeline
body: Staging environment, versioned releases, migrations run as part of deploy, pinned images (compose uses `postgres:latest`).

title: Make the app snappy
body:
General speed work, measured first so it goes where the time actually is.

- [ ] Measure: request timings in logs, Postgres slow query log, JS bundle size per route
- [ ] Stock balance table: `inventory_view` (migration 38) sums all of `stock_movement` on every read, which slows down as data grows. Keep a balance per product (and later per batch and branch) updated in the same transaction
- [ ] Indexes for the hot queries (product search, sales history, dashboard)
- [ ] Cache the product catalog in the browser so POS search is instant
- [ ] Optimistic updates and prefetching for the common screens; pagination on every long list
- [ ] Compression and long cache headers for the embedded static assets

title: Purchase order robustness
body:
Small fixes that keep purchase orders correct under retries, races and edits.

- [ ] Idempotency key for creating an order: Save is disabled while saving, but a retry after a lost response can still create a duplicate
- [ ] One shared lock-and-check helper: edit, close, move and receive each call `GetPurchaseOrderForUpdateTx` and compare the version themselves in `service/purchase_orders.go`
- [ ] Block changing or clearing the supplier on an order that already has receipts (today it's allowed silently and the receipts keep the old supplier); point to Move outstanding instead

title: Responsive mobile & tablet support
body:
Every screen works on phones and tablets, not just desktop.

- [ ] POS usable on a tablet; stock-take counting and receiving on a phone
- [ ] Dashboard, approvals and reports readable on a phone for owners
- [ ] Collapsible navigation, touch-sized controls, tables that become cards on small screens
- [ ] Known issue: purchase order card actions wrap below about 1280px

A native mobile app can come later through the PWA / app shell in T-094.

title: Customizable loyalty program
body:
Loyalty rules an admin sets up per store, instead of one fixed scheme.

- [ ] Earn rate (points per ₦ spent), with multipliers or exclusions by category or product (e.g. exclude prescription-only items)
- [ ] Redemption value, minimum to redeem, and points expiry
- [ ] Optional tiers with their own rates, and bonuses (birthday, first purchase, promotions)
- [ ] Points balance on the receipt and at the POS; redeem as a payment method
- [ ] Every earn, redeem and manual change audited

title: Tax / VAT support
body: Configurable tax rates for retail beyond medicines: tax-inclusive or exclusive pricing, exempt products, tax on receipts and in reports. Medical and pharmaceutical products are VAT-exempt in Nigeria, so for a pharmacy this mostly matters for non-drug items (cosmetics, toiletries, groceries) and for selling the system to other kinds of retailers. Check current rules with an accountant before building.

title: Change-due modal after saving a sale
body: Show a modal with the change to give when change > 0 after saving a sale.

title: Purchase order history search & filters
body: Search and filter by supplier, status and date, with pagination; the Completed tab is capped at the newest 100.

title: Approval workflow refinements
body:
- [ ] A drafter can withdraw a submitted order back to draft
- [ ] A manager can send an order back for changes instead of only rejecting it
- [ ] A rejected draft shows "Rejected" and its reason on the order itself, not "Closed" with the reason only in the activity log
- [ ] Tell the drafter when their order is approved, sent back or rejected (through T-103)

body: Generate and print barcode/shelf labels for products without manufacturer barcodes.

title: Product search returns stock as 0
body: `/inventory/search` results always carry `stock: 0`; only `/inventory/product/{id}` and `/inventory/item-list` compute it. Either compute it in the search query or drop the field so nothing relies on it. The POS uses item-list and isn't affected. Found in T-050.

There is no JS tooling today.

title: Require expected_stock for "set" stock adjustments
body:
CLAUDE.md says a "set" line sends `expected_stock` and is refused (409) if stock moved, but `CreateStockAdjustment` only checks it when the field is present (`service/stock_adjustments.go`, the `p.expected != nil` guard). The page always sends it; an API caller that omits it applies the absolute count over whatever stock is current, so a sale or receipt between the count and the save is overwritten. Raised by the review of T-113; the code was merged in T-050.

- [ ] Refuse a "set" line without `expected_stock` (400, plain message)
- [ ] Test: set without expected_stock is refused; with a stale value it is a 409; with the current value it is applied

title: Check the unverified findings from the T-113 review
body:
The review of T-113 also flagged merged code that was not part of that PR. None of these was checked; for each, confirm in code, then fix it or close it with a line saying why.

- [ ] `retryOf` (`service/stock_adjustments.go`) names another user's adjustment id when a retry key was already used by someone else; decide whether that should be a plain "already saved" message
- [ ] `productStockSQL` (`repository/stock_adjustments.go`) is a Sprintf template with `%%` escapes; check every use goes through Sprintf, or turn it into a function that takes the id expression
- [ ] `middleware/csrf.go` and `AuthMiddleware` now send JSON for anything but an HTML page load; check a PDF opened in an embed or iframe, and a classic form POST, still behave (5e3839a made this change on purpose)
- [ ] The comment in `service/inventory.go` (receiving) says products are locked in id order; check that the sort gives the lock order it claims, and that sorting `params.Products` in place does not matter to a caller
- [ ] `usePolledCounts` `start()` does nothing when the permission is not yet loaded; permissions come from `window.__PERMISSIONS__` at load, so this is probably fine, but confirm

title: What's new: release slideshow
body: A "What's new" button in the sidebar opens a slideshow of the newest release's features, each with a real screenshot, with a "New" badge (a dot when the sidebar is collapsed) until that person opens it. It is remembered per person in the browser and never pops up at sign-in. Slides are filtered by permission (an admin sees 5 for v0.3.0, a manager 4, a cashier 3), and the dialog has Back/Next, dots, arrow keys, Esc, a focus trap and works at phone width. The pictures are screens of the app running on made-up data: `go run ./cmd/demoseed` fills a local, empty database (it refuses anything else), and `docs/whats-new/` explains how to add a release's slides and retake the pictures. Also: `PHARMACY_PORT` sets the listen port (default 8000) and a failed listen now stops the server with the error. Plan: `docs/plans/T-113-whats-new.md`.

title: Reprint a receipt from sales history
body: Sales History has a "Reprint receipt" button on every sale (also fully returned ones). It opens a preview and prints a copy marked `*** REPRINT <time> ***`, laid out for an 80mm thermal roll, with returned items listed; the reprint is recorded in the audit log (`sale` / `receipt_reprinted`) before anything prints. POS and reprint slips now share one template (`lib/receipt.js`, escaped, printed through a hidden frame so no popup is blocked) and the POS slip carries the server's real receipt number instead of a made-up one; `POST /sales/` returns it, and a retried sale returns the first save's number. A failed print at the POS no longer leaves the cart full. Also fixed: a sold product with no manufacturer crashed Sales History. The customer name is not on reprints (not stored, T-040). Split from T-048. Plan: `docs/plans/T-112-reprint-receipt.md`.

title: Manual stock management
body: The app had no way to change stock except a full stock take; the product edit form had dropped its stock field, though the API still accepted a silent one. Managers (`stock:adjust`) now adjust stock in Inventory → Stock Adjustments. They can set a counted quantity or add/remove an amount, for several products at once, optionally correcting the expiry date. Every adjustment needs a reason (expired, damaged, theft or loss, count correction, opening stock, internal use, other) and records who, when, before and after, and the cost at the time. It's audited, products are locked so concurrent changes queue, stock can't go below zero, a retried save is applied once (one key per form; the server checks a resend is the same request from the same person), and products already counted in an open stock taking are refused. Cashiers (`stock:flag`) flag products for checking, optionally with the count they saw; one open flag per person per product. When a manager adjusts from a flag, the line starts at today's stock and shows what the cashier counted and what the system said then; the manager enters the count. Managers adjust from it (resolving it) or dismiss it; a product's open flags also show when it's added another way, and resolve only if the manager ticks that the adjustment answers them. Product edit no longer takes a stock value. Also fixed: `RequirePermissions` in "any" mode let requests with none of the permissions through. Follow-ups: T-107 to T-111. Plan: `docs/plans/T-050-manual-stock-management.md`.

title: Lock down public user registration
body: Removed public `POST /user/register`. Admins add users in Administration → Users → Add user (`POST /admin/api/users`, behind `admin:access`, audited). The first admin on a new install comes from the `create-admin` subcommand of the executable. Passwords need 10+ characters, must not be on the bundled NCSC common-password list and must not contain the username as a word; the admin reset uses the same rule and now stores the password as typed. Plan: `docs/plans/T-018-lock-down-registration.md`.

title: Purchase order approval workflow
body: Cashiers write drafts and submit them; managers approve or reject (with a reason), and their own orders skip approval. States `draft` → `pending_approval` → `open` or `closed`. Permissions `purchaseorder:draft` and `purchaseorder:approve`. Drafts are visible only to their author and approvers, can't be received against, and their PDF is stamped DRAFT. Every transition checks the order version and writes an audit entry. Approver badge and dashboard banner. Also: shared `ConfirmDialog` and `SupplierInput`, order card redesign, PDF watermarks. Migrations 000042, 000043.

title: Seed purchase order permissions
body: Migration 000043 seeds `PurchaseOrder`/`Draft` (Cashier) and `PurchaseOrder`/`Approve` (Manager, Admin), so there is no manual permission step at deploy.

title: Database integration test harness
body: `internal/testdb` creates/drops a database per test and runs real migrations; enabled with `PHARMACY_TEST_DSN`. Covers migrations and the purchase order lifecycle.

title: Audit log foundation
body: Append-only `audit_log` (a trigger blocks UPDATE/DELETE) written in the same transaction as the change: who, when, reason, before/after. Only purchase orders use it so far. Migration 000041.

title: Purchase orders & suppliers
body: Build an order from search, low-stock items or items not yet in the product list; edit, export a PDF, close with a reason, or move outstanding quantities to another supplier. Receiving against an order pre-fills outstanding quantities and rejects over-receiving. `supplier` table (find-or-create, case-insensitive, backfilled from receipts). Edits carry the order version. Writes need `purchaseorder:create`. Migration 000040.

title: Vue SPA / new UI
body: Migrated from Go templates to a Vue 3 + shadcn-vue SPA served under `/app/`, embedded in the Go binary.

title: Point of Sale
body: Prefix search on name/barcode/manufacturer, cart with price-option per line, discounts, split payments (Cash/Card/Transfer), server-generated receipt numbers, print receipt, idempotent submission, leave-with-cart guard.

title: Low stock & expiring items pages
body: Dedicated Low Stock and Expiring pages with PDF export (jsPDF).

title: Authentication & sessions
body: Login page (built before PRs were used), Argon2id password hashing, gorilla/sessions cookie sessions (expire at 3am), CSRF via gorilla/csrf with `GET /csrf-token` for the SPA.

title: Stock taking
body: Named stock-take sessions, live multi-user counting over WebSocket, dispensary + store counts, notes, expiry correction; completing (`stock:complete`) posts IN/OUT stock-taking adjustments.

title: Receiving (goods-in)
body: Receive supplier deliveries with cost price and expiry per line; hold/resume a receiving; received-items history; idempotency keys prevent duplicate receipts.

title: Role-based access control & admin panel
body: Roles (Admin/Manager/Cashier), permissions and role-permission assignment. Admin panel (`admin:access`): users (change role, reset password), roles, permissions, categories.

title: Dashboard
body: KPIs with period-over-period trend, sales trend chart, category split, top sellers, expiring items, expiry by category, low stock, recent transactions; date filter.

title: Product catalog
body: Products with category, barcode, manufacturer, reorder level, cost price. Multiple price options per product (e.g. tablet vs pack, `quantity_per_unit`) with a default. Edit product incl. manual stock adjustment (`inventory:edit`).

title: Sales history
body: Browse sales by date range and search, item and payment detail, net period total (minus refunds) gated by `salestotal:view`.

title: Returns
body: Return items against an original sale; stock goes back in (`IN_SALE_RETURN`); returns shown on the sale.

title: Stock export to CSV
body:
`GET /inventory/report/stock` CSV export.

Note: the new SPA no longer links to it.

title: Hold & resume sales
body: Park an in-progress sale and resume or void it from the Held Sales page.
